text:
olivia: heads-up, we’re seeing a new pattern of streaming gRPC truncation on hosted inference. clients get mid-response resets.
marcos: saw this at 09:12 UTC, ~0.6% of streams on region-eu are failing with truncated tokens and client errors.
vikas: logs show RST_STREAM and some GOAWAYs from the edge proxy. ALB target health is green.
jane: any NAT/egress spikes? conntrack logs?
olivia: yes — simultaneous spike in SNAT port exhaustion across edge NAT nodes around the same window.
marcos: interesting — I also see increased retransmits and bursts of tiny TCP windows before reset.
vikas: hypothesis: proxy buffer fills, sends WINDOW_UPDATE incorrectly or closes stream when backend stalls, and NAT port reuse turns the reset into a new 5xx path.
olivia: sample dump (trimmed):
```
[GRPC] stream id=125 RST_STREAM (0x0) -> client sees truncated response
[TCP] seq jump, src_port reused after 2s
```
infra-oncall: collecting pcaps + conntrack snapshots from affected hosts: /var/tmp/edge-nat-1865-2026.pcap.gz
jane: config check — ALB idle timeout=60s, proxy keepalive=30s, client keepalive=25s. mismatch could cause mid-stream kills when slow token generation happens.
marcos: also saw a correlation with long tail token generation (LLM backpressure). GPU tasks stall waiting on kv cache, backend spends extra seconds producing next chunks.
olivia: impact: lots of aborted streams -> inference jobs restart -> lower GPU occupancy and more overall token cost.
vikas: quick mitigation: 1) bump proxy keepalive to 90s on canary nodes, 2) enable prefix KV cache on model pool to reduce tail stalls, 3) add short-lived SNAT pool expansion to avoid port reuse.
jane: can we rollout 1) to a small subset? config flag ready: `edge.proxy.keepalive_secs=90`
marcos: will run canary in eu-west-1 with traffic split 5% -> 95% tomorrow 08:00 UTC. monitor: stream reset rate, p99 latency, conntrack allocation.
infra-oncall: incident INC-2026-219 opened, paging SRE-oncall if reset rate > 0.5% for 10m :pager:
sre-bot: acknowledged INC-2026-219
olivia: thanks — follow-up: if mitigation reduces resets we’ll plan a cluster-wide rollout + NAT pool size change. tracking in #eng-platform-ops.
